how: Forward P/E 16.9, VIX 11.8. Margin debt, small caps and four sectors had already peaked. The index fell 19.8% from here in 65 sessions.
Gains reversed after the statement; Dow −107. The forecast still showed three more rises in 2019.

t: Powell: rates “a long way from neutral”
how: Said after the close, on the day of the Dow’s record and oil’s four-year high. The 10-year yield went from 3.05% to 3.23% by 5 Oct; stocks broke a week later.
Third down day in a row, technology weakest. Payrolls +134,000, unemployment 3.7%.
Fifth straight loss; the Nasdaq’s worst day since 2016. JPMorgan blamed option hedging. The VIX closed above the three-month VIX for the first time.

t: Soft inflation report: morning rally sold
how: Dow −546. Recovery attempts failed all afternoon.
All sectors rose on bank and health-care results. The gain was being sold again two sessions later.

t: Caterpillar and 3M warn on costs and outlook
how: Dow −549 intraday, closed −126. The recovery did not hold: −3.1% the next day.
Texas Instruments reported slowing demand. Nasdaq −4.4%, its worst day since August 2011; chip index −6.6%. Close 2,656.10.

t: Amazon and Alphabet miss on revenue
how: Amazon −7.8%. The index traded more than 10% below its high intraday. FactSet: companies that had beaten estimates were down 1.5% on average.

t: Tariff report reverses a strong open: October low
how: Close 2,641.25 after a 900-point Dow range. The index then rallied 6.5% in seven sessions.

t: Strong jobs report; Apple −6.6% on its outlook
how: Payrolls +250,000. The Dow opened +200, fell to −300 and closed lower. Apple also stopped reporting unit sales.
+2.1%, the best day after a midterm election since 1982. It was the high of the rally, +6.5% from 29 Oct.

t: Fed holds, tone unchanged; 10-year peaks at 3.24%
how: Oil closed lower for a tenth day and entered a bear market. The rally stalled here and failed over the next two weeks.
Nasdaq nearly −3%. The index weakened all session.

t: Nvidia −19% after cutting its revenue outlook
how: Blamed unsold graphics cards after the crypto-mining boom. It fell another 12% the next session and 54% in the quarter.

t: All five FAANG stocks 20% or more off their highs
how: Facebook −38.8% and Netflix −36.1% from their highs. The relative strength of growth funds against the index made its low this day, 23 sessions before the index low.

t: Retailers sold on good results; Dow −550
how: Target, Ross and TJX fell despite higher sales and profits. Put/call ratio only 0.92: no panic yet.
Half-session after Thanksgiving. A new closing low; the index then rallied 6.0% to 3 Dec. Equity put/call 0.85.
+2.3%, but more stocks made 52-week lows than highs. Futures cut 2019 pricing to about one rate rise.

t: G20 tariff truce: gap up; first yield-curve inversion
how: Truce agreed on Saturday 1 Dec. +1.1%, the high of the rally (+6.0% from 23 Nov). The 5-year yield fell below the 3-year.

t: S&P 500 −3.2%: truce doubts and the yield curve
how: The whole truce rally was erased in one session.
Markets had been closed on 5 Dec. The recovery did not hold: −2.3% the next day.
Payrolls +155,000. Opened mixed and sold all day; the main indexes lost 3.7% to 4.2% on the week.

t: October low broken intraday, then reversed
how: Closed slightly higher. The reversal failed four sessions later.
AAII survey: most bears since 2013. $46.2bn left US stock funds in the week. The low was still eight sessions away.

t: China data, J&J −10%: lowest close since April
how: −1.9% to 2,599.95. Tax-loss selling accelerated from this day, by DataTrek’s account.
−2.1% to 2,545.94; the Russell 2000 was 20% below its high. The VIX stayed above the three-month VIX from here to 3 Jan.

t: Fed raises rates; runoff on “automatic pilot”
how: Dow +300 before the decision, −352 at the close. Cutting the 2019 forecast from three rises to two did not help.
Afternoon collapse on the shutdown threat. NYSE stocks at 52-week lows above 40% of issues.

t: Options expiry: volume peak; Nasdaq down 20%
how: −2.1% to 2,416.58 on 15.18bn shares. Equity put/call 1.13, highest of the year. The index lost 7.05% on the week.
Followed the Treasury’s Sunday statement on bank liquidity and a presidential tweet against the Fed. −2.7%; VIX 36.07; utilities −4.3%.
No real news; pension funds had about $60bn of stock to buy. Session 1 after the low and a 90% up day.
Largest upward reversal since 2010. The low was not approached again.

t: Apple warning and ISM slump: the low holds
how: Apple cut its revenue forecast after the close on 2 Jan. −2.5%, closing 4.1% above the low with the VIX at 25.
+3.4% with seven NYSE advancers per decliner. Session 7 after the low. The VIX fell back below the three-month VIX.
Ten-day NYSE advances 2.37 times declines. The index had closed above its 20-day EMA two sessions earlier.
First US high-yield deal since 30 Nov. The spread had peaked on 3 Jan.

t: Tariff-relief report; first close above the 50-day
how: Session 16 after the low, +12.1%. Most of the gain held although the Treasury denied the report.

t: China’s slowest growth since 1990: one down day
how: The data came out on 21 Jan, a US holiday. Second-worst day of the month, with no follow-through.
+1.6%. Apple +6.8% after reporting the weak quarter it had warned about.

t: Software index at an all-time high
how: First major group at a record. The S&P 500 had closed above its 200-day average on 12 Feb, session 33, +16.7% from the low.

t: Fed: no rises in 2019; runoff to end in September
how: Yields fell sharply; stocks were mixed, with banks weak.
Read as a recession warning alongside weak European factory surveys; stocks fell on the day.

t: New record close, the first since 20 Sep 2018
how: 81 sessions after the low. The Nasdaq 100 and the chip index were already at records.
